* The tests are now skipped if the cipher is not supported.
* Tests are now split into testing encryption, decryption and decryption of
  corrupt ciphertexts.

CipherOutputStream has the unfortunate behaviour that a decryption failure
because of an incorrect tag results in an empty plaintext rather than an
exception.
Oracle isn't changing this:
http://www.oracle.com/technetwork/java/javase/8u171-relnotes-4308888.html

The main purpose of the test is to ensure that a provider does not behave
even worse by returning partial plaintext.

Before the CL tests pass if they return empty plaintext. With this CL
tests only pass if there is an exception and either fail or are skipped
if they return empty plaintext.

The corruption tests pass under jdk11 they are skipped under jdk19.

pr_title: Refactor assertTrue(!equals()) using assertNotEquals & @Test(excepted) using assertThrows
pr_body:
I am working on research that investigates test smell refactoring in which we identify alternative implementations of test cases, study how commonly used these refactorings are, and assess how acceptable they are in practice.

The first smell is when inappropriate assertions are used, while there exist better alternatives. For example, in [GuardProxyCatalogTest.java](https://github.com/apache/karaf/commit/d0456624885a9bff8d4418614b1e8469981c26c3#diff-de2cfbdc07af433a0de11f25b23069dabd16eba9eb4e3157701fbd89562c10b7), I refactored `assertTrue(!GuardProxyCatalog.PROXY_CREATOR_THREAD_NAME.equals(t.getName()));` using `assertNotEquals(GuardProxyCatalog.PROXY_CREATOR_THREAD_NAME, t.getName());`.

The second smell is when exception handling can alternatively be implemented using assertion rather than annotation. For example, in [EventSendCommandTest.java](https://github.com/apache/karaf/commit/100420f757c2bd6fe00a8d28c14a1388d665b8fe#diff-80c4f1284affb61c43d9458dcb2580b0c7d770415291e34238bfc238a7cf6451), I used `assertThrows(IllegalArgumentException.class, () -> {...});` instead of `@Test(expected=IllegalArgumentException.class)`.

While there could be several cases like this, we aim in this pull request to get your feedback on these particular test smells and their refactorings. Thanks in advance for your input.

## Description

<!-- Please explain the changes you made here. -->
This PR adds the termination logic to the process instance modification processor. When an element gets terminated we need to take care of a few things:

1. The job needs to be cancelled
2. Potential incidents needs to be resolved
3. Event subscriptions need to be cancelled

For the cancelling of event subscriptions I have reused the logic in the behavior classes we already have. This had one side-effect. Before timers got cancelled by sending a cancel command. In the case of PI modification we want to send an event instead of a command. Since the timer cancel command does nothing more than create the event Nico and I concluded that we might as well use an event here for all cases. As a result you will find a minor refactoring in this PR which changes the behavior to send a cancelled event instead of a cancel command. This also resulted in the deprecation of the cancel command.

pr_body:
## Description

Add support for BPMN terminate end events. See https://github.com/camunda/zeebe/issues/8789#issuecomment-1253338375 on how the BPMN element should work.

The implementation doesn't follow the BPMN spec in one point: the flow scope that contains the terminate end event is not terminated but completed. Reasoning:
- The state of the flow scope is a detail that doesn't influence the core behavior. In both cases, the process instance should continue, for example, by taking the outgoing sequence flow. The difference is not visible to process participants but only when monitoring the process instance, for example, in Operate.
- It fits better with the existing implementation. It would be a bigger effort to continue the process instance (e.g. taking the outgoing sequence flow) when the flow scope is terminated. As a result, we would end up in more complex code.
- It aligns with the behavior of Camunda Platform 7. 

Side note: I implemented the major parts during a [Live Hacking session](https://www.twitch.tv/videos/1584245006). :movie_camera: 

## Related issues

closes #8789

>The implementation doesn't follow the BPMN spec in one point: the flow scope that contains the terminate end event is not terminated but completed.

pr_title: Build under Java 11, update library and plugin versions.
pr_body:
We recently found a successful path to update OTP to build under Java 11: no module-info file, only adding an automatic-module-name to the JAR manifest via some Maven config, and allowing "illegal" reflective access with JVM switches only within the test runner.

I have applied these same changes to R5 in this pull request. As part of the migration to java 11, several dependencies and Maven plugins had to move to new versions. Of course this cascades other dependency version changes and creates possible conflicts.

Currently this PR does not compile because R5 dependencies (specifically gtfs-lib) are using the old JTS package name, but JTS has moved to the org.locationetch package hierarchy. So this PR is on hold until R5's dependencies to also migrate to Java 11 and bump all their dependency versions. Ideally we should cross-check that the whole dependency tree across projects (OTP, R5, gtfs-lib, osm-lib) is aligned on version numbers, including things like Protobuf, JTS, and Geotools, but also any others we spot.

### Description

This PR adds functionality for normalizing strings in a GTFS table:
- Capitalize strings, with exceptions
- Substitute text/words, with optional space normalization around words, if substituting words.
In addition:
- `ZipTransform` and `DbTransform` are refactored to pass the correct `FeedTransformTarget` type to the implementers

Things that have yet to be resolved:
- There is a "convert to sentence case" stub/option in `NormalizeFieldTransformation`, is it important?
- Should we support for the GTFS table files inside a folder in the GTFS ZIP archive? e.g. `gtfs.zip/google_transit/routes.txt`

pr_title: Adding boundary tag to nodes on ways that span boundaries
pr_body:
When a way is not assigned any country code (it is not within a country boundary) but it is still connected to ways that are inside the boundary (long bridges, ferry routes for example), the end nodes of those ways were not assigned any `synthetic_boundary_node` tag. This PR adds the tag to those nodes.
It also refactors the function that decides when an OSM node becomes an Atlas `Point`. That allows to take the new tags into account, and to avoid building more `Point`s than necessary.

commit_subject: [#452] HotFix: GitLogTest fails due to system time >= 2019  (#455)
commit_body:
GitLogTest#gitLog_sinceDateInFuture_noContent() test method has a check
which asserts that if the until date given is before any of the
repository's commit date, the git log command should not give any
commmit info.

However, after the new year in year 2019, the test now fails. This may
be due to the Year 2038[1] problem. As the given until date is too
early (year 1950), this causes the time difference to overflow. As
such, a future until date is formed instead, causing git log to give
all the commit info, thus the test fails.

As a hotfix for this issue, let's set an earlier until date
(year 2010) for the test instead.

As this check is also not within the scope of the test method,
gitLog_sinceDateInFuture_noContent(), let's refactor it out to
a different test method, gitLog_untilDateBeforeAnyCommit_noContent.

[1]: Description of the Year 2038 problem:
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Year_2038_problem
